Content

The proposals were rejected by INC. Gandhi famously referred Cripps offer of Dominion Status as "post-dated cheque drawn on a failing bank".

QUIT INDIA MOVEMENT 1942

  • July 1942: The Congress Working Committee met at Wardha, Maharashtra where Quit India Resolution was adopted. It was ratified at Gowalika Tank, Bombay.

Quit India Movement

  • On 8th August 1942, Mahatma Gandhi launched Quit India Movement (also known as August Kranti) in response to the failure of Cripps Mission, which was initially not supported by J L Nehru and Hindu Mahasabha.
  • The "Do or Die" slogan was given during a speech by Mahatma Gandhi at the Gowalia Tank Maidan or August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai. The slogan was a call to action for Indians to fight for independence from British rule.
  • The very first day all leaders got arrested and that is why this movement was a leaderless movement.
  • Aruna Asaf Ali presided over Congress Working Committee, she also hoisted the Indian Flag at the Gowalika Tank in Mumbai.

Specific Appeals made by Gandhi (during the Quit India Movement)

  • To government servants Gandhi advised not to resign from their posts but instead urged them to remain loyal to the cause of the INC and work against British policies subtly.
  • Soldiers were instructed not to resign from their duties but were urged to refuse orders to fire on fellow compatriots.
  • Gandhi appealed to peasants to withhold rent payments if the landlords or Zamindars were loyal to the British government.
  • He encouraged the people living in princely states to support their ruler if the ruler was anti-British. If the ruler was pro-British, Gandhi advised them to peacefully oppose the government.

Martyrs

  • Kushal Konwar was the only martyr of the Quit India phase of the freedom movement who was hanged.
  • Kanaklata Barua was shot dead by the British forces while leading a procession during QIM.

Underground Activities Carried Out

  • Usha Mehta: Launched underground radio in Bombay and appealed Indians to join Quit India Movement.
  • Parallel government were setup:
  • In Ballia by: Chittu Pandey
  • In Tamluk by: Jatiya Sarkar
  • In Satara by: Prati Sarkar (Y B Chauhan, Nana Patil)
  • 23 March 1943: Pakistan Day was observed by Muslim League.
  • The term PAKISTAN was coined in 1933 by Rahmat Ali.

Lahore Resolution

  • Lahore Resolution: It is also called as Pakistan Resolution was a formal political statement adopted by the All-India Muslim League on the occasion of its three-day general session in Lahore, Punjab, from 22 to 24 March 1940, calling for a separate homeland for the Muslims of British India.

Mediation between Congress and Muslim League

  • 1944: C. Rajagopalachari gave C R Formula (Clement-Read Formula) in response to the growing tensions between the INC and the Muslim League.
  • Desai Liaquat Pact 1945: It was an unsuccessful agreement between Bhalubhai Desai (from Congress) and Liaquat Ali Khan (from Muslim League).
  • 1945: Wavell Plan was proposed by then Viceroy Lord Archibald Wavell as an attempt to resolve the political deadlock between the INC and the Muslim League. This plan was discussed in Shimla Conference; however it failed.

Atomic Bomb (FYI)

In September 1945, World War II completely ended with the US bombings. In August 1945, US bombed in Hiroshima and Nagasaki (two cities of Japan) on 6 August and 9 August respectively. The bomb dropped on Hiroshima was known as "Little Boy". While the bomb dropped on Nagasaki was known as "Fat Man" which was more powerful than the "Little Boy" and that is from where we came up with the idea of naming this book and our GK MCQ Book (Little Boy).

INDIAN NATIONAL ARMY (INA)

  • The Indian National Army (INA) was founded during World War II to fight against British rule in India.
  • It was initially formed in 1942 by Mohan Singh with Indian Prisoners of Wars in Singapore (it was later handed to Rash Behari Bose who again transferred the leadership to S C Bose).

Subash Chandra Bose

  • He was born in Cuttack on 23rd Jan 1897.
  • In 1942, he met Hitler in Germany (he had earlier travelled to Berlin in April 1941 using the Italian passport of "Orlando Mazzotta").
  • The Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) was reorganised by Bose in Singapore in 1943.
  • He founded "Free India Legion/Tiger Legion" in 1941 in Berlin, Germany.
  • He formed a women regiment named after Rani Lakshmibai led by Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan.
  • On 15th August, Japan surrendered to Allied powers, marking the end of World War II.
  • He died on: 18th August in a plane crash.
  • S C Bose was called as "Patriot of Patriots" by Gandhi.
  • In 1944, he was the person to give "Father of Nation" title to Gandhi through Singapore Radio.

Famous Slogans by S C Bose

  • "Delhi Chalo"
  • "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom"
  • "Jai Hind"
Birth anniversary of S.C. Bose is celebrated every year as "Parakram Divas".
The Indian struggle 1920-1942 was authored by S C Bose.

INA trials

  • The Indian National Army trials (also known as the INA trials and the Red Fort trials) was the British Indian trial by court-martial of a number of officers of the Indian National Army (INA) between November 1945 and May 1946.
  • First INA trial was held against: Prem Kumar Sehgal, Shah Nawaz Khan and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon in Red Fort in 1945.
  • Congress came in defence of these INA soldiers and formed a committee which included Jawaharlal Nehru, Bhulabhai Desai, Asaf Ali, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Kailash Nath Katju, and others.
  • 14th February 1946: The ratings (sailors in lowest rank) of Royal Indian Navy (RIN) revolted against British due to the discrimination and poor conditions and this led to a historic Royal Indian Navy Mutiny. This event began at the HMIS Talwar (a shore establishment in Bombay) against the poor working conditions (low pay, poor food quality, etc.).

CABINET MISSION PLAN

  • In 1945, elections were held in Britain where Labour Party under the leadership of Clement Atlee formed the government.
  • In March 1946, Clement Attlee (then PM of Britain) sent a delegation called the Cabinet Mission consisting of:
  • Lord Pethick-Lawrence (Chairman), Sir Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander.
  • It proposed a 3-tiered Federal Plan.

Provisions in Cabinet Mission Plan

  • The plan proposed a united India, rejecting the demand for a separate Pakistan.
  • The Cabinet Mission Plan proposed a three-tier administrative structure for British India, with the Federal Union at the top tier, individual provinces at the bottom tier and Groups of provinces as a middle tier.
  • Provincial were divided into three groups:
  • Group A: Hindu-majority provinces (Madras, Bombay, UP, Bihar, Odisha, Central Provinces)
  • Group B: Muslim-majority provinces (Punjab, NWFP, Sindh, Balochistan)
  • Group C: Bengal and Assam
  • Central Government to have power over defense, foreign affairs, and communications.
  • Provinces to have full autonomy and residual powers.
  • Princely States were free to negotiate their status, either to join with Britishers or Successor Governments.
  • Constituent Assembly to draft a new constitution; members would be elected by provincial assemblies.
  • Interim Government to function till the new constitution and government were formed.

Response to the Cabinet Mission Plan

  • Indian National Congress: It accepted the plan partially but opposed the idea of grouping, fearing it was a step toward partition.
  • Muslim League: It initially accepted the plan though it did not have a separate provision for Pakistan, thinking that the provision for grouping will provide it a separate Nation but when Jinnah sensed that this grouping is not mandatory then he called for "Direct Action Day".
  • The Muslim League Observed "Day of Deliverance" on 22 December 1939.

MOUNTBATTEN PLAN

  • The Mountbatten Plan which formed the basis for Indian Independence Act proposed for the Partition of India into two Dominions namely India and Pakistan. That's why it is also known as Partition Plan.
  • Under this Plan, the Princely States were given the option to join either India or Pakistan or remain Independent.
  • Out of 565 Princely States, 563 joined either India or Pakistan and 3 did not join initially. They were: J & K, Hyderabad and Junagarh.
  • Louis Mountbatten: Last Governor-General of India.
  • C. Rajagopalachari: Only Governor-General of independent India (because later this post was removed).
  • Bangladesh Liberation War in 1971 led to the separation of East Pakistan (now Bangladesh) from West Pakistan (now Pakistan). This war took place during the tenure of Indira Gandhi.
  • In 1972, the Shimla Agreement was signed by Indira Gandhi (then PM) and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto (then President of Pakistan) to restore peace between two countries. It has been suspended by Pakistan in a move of retaliation after India suspended Indus Water Treaty.
Note: To see Provisions of Indian Independence act 1947 refer to chapter "Important Acts" in Polity section.
